I want to build a singleplayer game that I can host using github pages. This will be a single player game so we only need to build the frontend. I want to use bun for this project. I want to use react for the UI and canvas 2d for the game rendering. We can use typescript for the bulk of the coding. 

Here's the high level overview for the game. This will play like a roguelike/rpg. We start with a menu with "start" or "continue". Continue is disabled unless a save file is detected in local.  In either case the player will then be presented with 3 character options to start the game, A player can only pick the first class at the start and will need to unlock the others by playing. After picking their character they go into combat with a random enemy from a pool of enemies meant for the first round. After winning they level up which allows them to put a point into one of three talent trees. Talent trees give passives and access to new abilities. The combat is pseudo turn based, the player will auto attack based on their attack speed. The player will have a selector hovering which enemy they're targetting and can swap targets on the fly with the arrow keys. Enemies also have an auto attack time, however theirs will be a range so their auto attack times will differ slightly between attacks. The player will have abilities they can activate at anytime which typically interact with their auto attack timer doing things like buffing the next auto attack, interrupting the auto attack and instantly doing something, pausing the auto attack bar to do something, and other things that will be designed as we go on. Enemies will have similar abilities they will automatically use throughout combat. 

This is the basic loop for the game, in the future we'll want to add more things like going to town inbetween battles before going into combat again, crafting, items/equipment, a shop, enemy item drops, and quests.

I want to go over the plan for building this game. so we can organize tasks correctly and develop smoothly.

## Plan: Roguelike/RPG Browser Game with React + Canvas 2D

Build a GitHub Pages-hosted singleplayer roguelike with pseudo-turn-based combat, featuring auto-attack timers, abilities, talent trees, and character progression. Architecture separates game logic (pure TypeScript) from React UI, with Canvas 2D for rendering.

---

### Steps

1. **Scaffold project with Bun + Vite + React + TypeScript** — Initialize with `bun create vite`, configure `vite.config.ts` with `base` for GitHub Pages deployment, set up folder structure separating `game/`, `rendering/`, and `ui/` directories.

2. **Build core game loop and time system** — Implement `requestAnimationFrame` loop with fixed timestep for logic updates, store game instance in React `useRef`, create `GameBridge` hook to sync UI-relevant state at controlled intervals (~10-15 FPS).

3. **Create game state architecture** — Design plain TypeScript state objects for `Player`, `Enemy`, `Combat`, `Progression`. Include serializable save format with version field for localStorage persistence. Consider lightweight ECS pattern for entities with varied behaviors.

4. **Implement main menu and character select screens** — React components for "Start" / "Continue" buttons (Continue disabled without save), character class picker with unlock system tied to saved progression data.

5. **Build combat system with auto-attack timers** — Implement `CooldownComponent` pattern: player/enemy attack timers decrement each tick, trigger attacks when reaching zero. Add target selector (arrow key navigation), variable enemy attack ranges, and ability interrupt/buff hooks.

6. **Create Canvas 2D rendering layer** — Renderer class that draws combat scene (player, enemies, health bars, attack timer visualizations, ability cooldown indicators), subscribed to game state, rendered each animation frame.

7. **Implement talent tree and level-up system** — Post-combat level-up screen with 3 talent branches, state for unlocked talents/abilities, passive effect system that modifies combat stats.

8. **Set up GitHub Actions deployment** — Workflow to build with Bun and deploy `dist/` to `gh-pages` branch on push to main.

---

### Further Considerations

1. **ECS vs simple classes for entities?** Lightweight ECS offers flexibility for status effects, varied enemy behaviors, and item modifiers — recommended for this genre. Or start simpler and refactor later?

2. **Art/asset strategy?** Use placeholder shapes/colors initially, or source free pixel art assets? This affects canvas rendering complexity.

3. **Balance data storage?** Keep enemy stats, ability values, talent effects in JSON data files (easy tuning) vs TypeScript constants? JSON recommended for iteration speed.

4. **Scope for MVP?** Suggest first milestone: Menu → 1 playable class → 3 enemy types → 2 abilities → 1 talent branch → save/load. Add classes, enemies, talents incrementally. Does this phasing work for you?

Based on my research and expert knowledge, here's a comprehensive summary for planning your roguelike/RPG browser game:

---

## 1. Project Structure

**Recommended folder structure:**

```
src/
├── game/                    # Pure game logic (framework-agnostic)
│   ├── core/                # Game loop, time management
│   ├── ecs/                 # Entity Component System (optional)
│   │   ├── components/      # Data-only component definitions
│   │   ├── systems/         # Logic systems (combat, movement, AI)
│   │   └── entities/        # Entity factories/templates
│   ├── state/               # Game state management
│   ├── combat/              # Combat calculations, cooldowns
│   ├── world/               # Map, dungeon generation
│   └── utils/               # Game-specific utilities
├── rendering/               # Canvas 2D rendering layer
│   ├── renderer.ts          # Main canvas renderer
│   ├── sprites/             # Sprite management
│   └── camera.ts            # Viewport/camera logic
├── ui/                      # React components (HUD, menus)
│   ├── components/          # UI components
│   ├── hooks/               # Custom React hooks for game integration
│   └── screens/             # Game screens (menu, inventory, etc.)
├── assets/                  # Static assets
└── index.tsx                # Entry point
```

**Key principle:** Keep `game/` completely decoupled from React. It should be pure TypeScript with no React dependencies, making it testable and portable.

---

## 2. Game Loop Architecture

**Pattern: Game loop outside React's control**

- Use `requestAnimationFrame` for the main loop, managed via `useRef` to store the loop handle
- The game loop should run independently of React's render cycle
- React only renders when UI state changes (health bars, inventory, etc.)

**Recommended approach:**
- **Fixed timestep for game logic** (~20-50ms ticks) with variable rendering
- Store `lastTick` and calculate `deltaTime` to keep simulation consistent
- Use `performance.now()` for high-resolution timing (passed by rAF as callback argument)

**Avoiding conflicts:**
- Game state lives in a plain TypeScript class/object, **not** in React state
- Use `useRef` to hold reference to the game instance
- Use `useEffect` only once to start/stop the game loop on mount/unmount
- Sync to React sparingly: push UI-relevant data via a subscription pattern or controlled `setState` calls

---

## 3. State Management

**Recommended pattern: Game state outside React**

| Layer | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| **Game State (core)** | Plain TypeScript objects/classes. Authoritative source of truth. Mutated directly in game loop. |
| **React State (UI)** | Minimal subset needed for UI. Updated via subscription or polling at controlled intervals. |

**ECS consideration:**
- ECS (Entity-Component-System) is excellent for roguelikes due to flexible entity composition
- Components are pure data; Systems contain logic and iterate over entities with matching components
- Libraries like **bitECS** (performance-focused) or **miniplex** (React-friendly) work well, or roll your own lightweight version
- For a roguelike, ECS shines for: enemies with varied behaviors, items with combinable effects, status effects, buff systems

**Sync strategy:**
- Subscribe UI components to specific state slices
- Use a `GameBridge` hook that reads from game state and triggers React updates at ~10-15 FPS for UI (not every frame)
- Avoid putting frequently-changing data (positions, animations) in React state

---

## 4. Bun + React Setup for GitHub Pages

**Setup steps:**

1. **Create project with Vite:**
   ```bash
   bun create vite my-roguelike
   # Select: React → TypeScript + SWC
   cd my-roguelike
   bun install
   ```

2. **Configure for GitHub Pages** in `vite.config.ts`:
   ```ts
   export default defineConfig({
     base: '/your-repo-name/',  // Required for GH Pages subpath
     plugins: [react()],
   })
   ```

3. **Update package.json scripts:**
   ```json
   "scripts": {
     "dev": "bunx --bun vite",
     "build": "bunx --bun vite build",
     "preview": "bunx --bun vite preview"
   }
   ```

4. **Deploy:** Output goes to `dist/`. Use GitHub Actions to build and push to `gh-pages` branch, or use `gh-pages` npm package.

**Why Vite:**
- Native TypeScript/TSX support
- Fast HMR during development
- Works seamlessly with Bun
- Simple static output for GitHub Pages

---

## 5. Save System Best Practices

**Core principles:**

| Concern | Recommendation |
|---------|----------------|
| **Serialization** | Use `JSON.stringify/parse`. Avoid storing class instances directly; serialize to plain objects. |
| **Versioning** | Always include a `version` field in save data. Write migration functions for breaking changes. |
| **Validation** | Use Zod or similar to validate loaded data against expected schema. |
| **Compression** | For large saves, consider `lz-string` library to compress before storing. |
| **Error handling** | Wrap in try/catch; localStorage can throw (quota exceeded, security restrictions). |

**TypeScript pattern:**
```ts
interface SaveData {
  version: number;
  player: PlayerState;
  world: WorldState;
  timestamp: number;
}
```

**Auto-save strategy:**
- Save on meaningful events (level complete, combat end)
- Debounce saves to avoid performance hits
- Consider multiple save slots with metadata for slot selection UI

**localStorage limits:** ~5-10MB per origin. For larger games, consider IndexedDB.

---

## 6. Combat System Patterns (Timer/Cooldown-based)

**Core architecture:**

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **CooldownComponent** | Stores `{ currentTime: number, duration: number }` for each ability |
| **CombatTimerSystem** | Each tick: decrement all cooldowns by `deltaTime`, trigger auto-attacks when ready |
| **Action Queue** | Queue player actions; execute when cooldown reaches 0 |

**Implementation approach:**
- Store cooldowns as **time remaining** (in ms or seconds)
- Each game loop tick: `cooldown.current = Math.max(0, cooldown.current - deltaTime)`
- When `cooldown.current === 0`, ability is ready
- On ability use: `cooldown.current = cooldown.duration`

**Auto-attack pattern:**
```
attackTimer -= deltaTime
if (attackTimer <= 0 && hasTarget) {
  performAttack()
  attackTimer = attackSpeed  // Reset
}
```

**Design considerations:**
- Use **time-based**, not frame-based cooldowns (handles variable FPS)
- For turn-based hybrid: accumulate "action points" over time instead
- Store cooldown durations in entity/ability data for easy balancing
- Consider speed stats as multipliers on cooldown duration

---

## Summary Recommendations

| Area | Key Takeaway |
|------|--------------|
| **Architecture** | Strict separation: game logic → rendering → React UI |
| **Game Loop** | `requestAnimationFrame` with fixed timestep logic, variable render |
| **State** | Game state in plain TS, sync to React only for UI; consider lightweight ECS |
| **Tooling** | Bun + Vite + React + TypeScript works great; simple deploy to GH Pages |
| **Saves** | Versioned JSON, validate on load, handle errors gracefully |
| **Combat** | Time-based cooldowns decremented in game loop, ability-ready checks |

## Plan: Roguelike/RPG Browser Game — MVP

Build a GitHub Pages-hosted roguelike with one playable class, a talent tree with 4 functional abilities + passives, an innate block ability, and 4 enemy types (tutorial dummy + 3 combat enemies). Uses custom TypeScript classes, Canvas shapes for visuals, and JSON for balance data.

---

### Steps

1. **Scaffold project with Bun + Vite + React + TypeScript** — Initialize project, configure for GitHub Pages, set up folder structure: `game/` (classes, combat, state), `rendering/` (canvas), `ui/` (React screens), `data/` (JSON configs for enemies, abilities, talents).

2. **Build core game loop and state management** — `Game` class with `requestAnimationFrame` loop, fixed timestep updates, `GameState` class holding player/enemy/combat state. React `GameBridge` hook syncs UI-relevant state. Save system with versioned JSON to localStorage.

3. **Implement Player and Enemy classes** — `Player` class with HP, attack timer, attack speed, stats, equipped abilities, applied passives. `Enemy` class with HP, variable attack timing (min/max range), abilities list. Both extend a shared `Combatant` base class.

4. **Build combat system with timer mechanics** — Attack timers decrement each tick, trigger auto-attacks at zero. Target selection with arrow keys. Implement innate block ability: pauses player attack timer for 0.5s, applies 50% damage reduction buff during duration.

5. **Create ability and passive systems** — `Ability` class with cooldown, effect type (instant, buff, attack modifier), execute logic. `Passive` class that modifies player stats on apply. Load definitions from JSON. Support ability hooks: `onAutoAttack`, `onTakeDamage`, `onActivate`.

6. **Design talent tree data structure and UI** — JSON schema for talent tree with nodes (ability or passive), prerequisites, unlock state. React component displaying tree with clickable nodes. First node unlocks the first ability. Most nodes are placeholders, 4 abilities + key passives functional.

7. **Implement 4 enemy types** — JSON definitions: (1) Tutorial Dummy — 1 HP, no attacks, instant kill; (2-4) Three combat enemies with varied HP, attack speed ranges, and at least one ability each. Enemy AI system that auto-uses abilities based on conditions.

8. **Create Canvas 2D renderer** — Draw combat scene with shapes: player (rectangle), enemies (circles/shapes by type), health bars, attack timer bars, ability cooldown indicators, target selector highlight. Keep styling minimal but readable.

9. **Build game flow screens** — React screens: Main Menu (Start/Continue), Character Select (1 class selectable, 2 locked placeholders), Combat View (canvas + ability bar + HP display), Level Up / Talent Tree overlay, Victory/Defeat modals.

10. **Implement progression loop** — Tutorial dummy fight → level up → unlock first talent (ability) → random enemy from pool → level up → talent point → repeat. Save progress after each combat. Load on Continue.

11. **Set up GitHub Actions deployment** — Workflow: on push to main, run `bun install && bun run build`, deploy `dist/` to `gh-pages` branch.

---

### Further Considerations

1. **Block ability activation?** Spacebar for block, number keys (1-4) for abilities? Or different binding preference?

2. **Talent tree shape?** Linear path with branches, or grid layout? Linear is simpler for MVP with one tree.

3. **Enemy pool scaling?** After tutorial, pick random enemy from all 3, or introduce them progressively (enemy 1 for rounds 2-3, add enemy 2 at round 4, etc.)?
